title: Eliminate artificial delays in C64 Krill boot and suspend (CRC-16 display check and settle loops)
description:
Audit and remove non-I/O CPU hangs perceived by users during Krill fast-loader operation.

Root Causes:
1. Display Memory CRC-16 Check: In platforms/commodore/c64/boot.s, boot_crc_baseline (line 254) and chain_crc_verify (line 720) each compute a software bit-by-bit CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over 10,000 bytes (8KB bitmap at $C000, 1KB screen matrix at $E000, 1KB color RAM at $D800).
   - At ~250 cycles/byte, each pass burns ~2.5 million CPU cycles (~2.5 seconds on 1MHz 6502) of pure spinlock with zero disk I/O.
   - First pass holds screen blank for 2.5s after bootart64 loads.
   - Second pass (chain_crc_verify) freezes the boot art on screen for 2.5s right after 64.BANK loads and immediately before the main menu is shown.
   - Missed in testing because VICE runs with --warp in CI/harnesses (~15ms execution time). Test harness (run_tests.sh) even asserts bit 7 of krill_boot_art_used=0x81.
2. Settle loop in krill_suspend: In platforms/commodore/c64/main.s:2857, a 4-page busy loop (4*256*256*5 cycles = 1.31M cycles = ~1.3s) executes with SEI whenever suspending Krill (Disk Setup menu, save slot prompt, death, victory).
3. Failover delay: chain_krill_fail waits 150 frames (2.5-3.0s) on error fallback.

Recommendations:
- Replace the 10,000-byte bit-by-bit CRC-16 in boot.s with fast canary byte probes (<1ms) or an additive XOR/sum checksum (~0.1s), or shift whole-span verification exclusively to the python test harness via VICE monitor inspection.
- Update test harness assertions (krill_boot_art_used bit 7) to match the new verification mechanism.
- Profile and reduce the 1.3s blind delay in krill_suspend to the minimal settle window required by 1541 DOS reset.
close_reason: Replaced boot-art CRC spins with boundary canaries plus full-span VICE verification; removed synchronous-uninstall settle spins; focused 22-scenario boot matrix and corrected static contracts pass.

comments.author: mr_spock
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW RESULT: REVISION REQUIRED. Implementation of moria8-x6t.1 must not proceed from Revision 2 as written. The selected core layout is viable: bitmap $C000-$DF3F, matrix $E000-$E3E7, MORIA64 ending at $BFFF, 64.BANK $F000-$FFF7, and post-blank 64.INIT $C000-$C368 are mutually safe in the happy-path phase ordering. The following blockers and gaps must be corrected first.

BLOCKERS

1. The chain stub does not fit at $0340. The current stub is 187 bytes in its 192-byte $0340-$03FF window, leaving 5 bytes; see boot.s:397-519. The new 64.INIT name alone is 8 bytes, before its load sequence, settle/evidence/blank operations, KERNAL fallback, and cleanup. Design section 8.4 estimates the current stub at about 130 bytes and is false. Required revision: provide and prove a new surviving stub/code/data location or a fully byte-counted redesign; retain the boundary assert.

2. The proposed two-load KERNAL path omits required channel cleanup. Existing load_boot_art closes logical file 2 because LOAD leaves it in the file table (boot.s:127-136). Revision 2 section 5.2 loads MORIA64 and then 64.INIT without CLOSE/CLRCHN between them or after successful 64.INIT, contradicting section 6.2. Required revision: specify CLOSE/CLRCHN and carry preservation for every successful and failed KERNAL LOAD, and include those bytes in the stub proof.

3. Krill install can corrupt KRES64 before first use on 1541U. Boot loads KRES64 to $0400 before jsr $2000 (boot.s:318-340). Krill r194 detects DRIVE_1541U and calls message (tools/krill/loader/src/install.s:719-724); message selects screen $0400 and calls BSOUT for the warning (install.s:781-815), then install returns success (install.s:726-733). This overwrites executable resident bytes at $0400-$04ED. Required revision: preserve a clean resident across install or place/copy it only after all install messages, with exact ownership and copy proof. Also correct the P1 claim that display remains blank: the vendor warning and mute-device error renderer explicitly enable text display. This is also tracked by moria8-gh1.

4. Mid-boot Krill recovery can visibly select garbage. Current recovery writes $DD00=$03 while $D011 may still be bitmap-on (boot.s:433-464). Revision 2 requires bank 3 via $DD00=$00, so a MORIA64/64.BANK failure switches the live VIC to unrelated bank-0 bitmap data for the 150-frame wait and KERNAL retry. Required revision: define an ordering that blanks before changing banks, or safely retains/restores the art; do not claim recovery follows the art-live fallback unless it does.

5. NMI safety is not proved. Section 6.2 says no NMI source is enabled but acknowledges RESTORE NMI during $01=$35/$30; SEI does not mask NMI. Before main installs RAM vectors, an NMI in the all-RAM copy window vectors through unproved RAM at $FFFA/$FFFB. Required revision: install/protect a safe RAM NMI route around these windows or provide source-backed proof that no source can assert. Calling this an accepted pre-existing risk does not satisfy the design acceptance criterion.

HIGH/MEDIUM REQUIRED CORRECTIONS

6. KINST64 span is wrong. The current artifact is 6998 bytes including the $2000 header, so it writes 6996 bytes at $2000-$3B53, not $2000-$2C98 as sections 4 and 7 state. The corrected span remains compatible with the selected layout but the ownership proof must use it.

7. Non-device-8 fallback is unproved and currently fails structurally. Boot accepts devices 8-30 and uses boot_device (boot.s:138-146, 304-329), but fallback 64.BANK uses program_device (main.s:2638-2653), initialized to 8 (common/disk_swap.s:27-30) with no C64 adoption of boot_device. Required revision: either carry the boot device into program_device before init_load_banked or explicitly narrow and enforce supported boot devices; add a real device-9 scenario if support is retained.

8. Verification is insufficient for stated failure preservation. $033B=$3B proves register state only, not bitmap/matrix/color integrity. Add a production-path checkpoint after MORIA64 and 64.BANK but before blanking that validates representative boundaries or a checksum of $C000-$DF3F, $E000-$E3E7, and color RAM. Add injected scenarios for loadraw failure at MORIA64, 64.BANK, and 64.INIT; missing BOOTART64; KERNAL 64.INIT failure; and the 1541U warning path. At minimum each distinct recovery transition must execute. The exact authoritative gate remains make test64, but moria8-dp6 documents that it cannot currently complete under the mandatory 30-second cap; the implementation cannot claim completion until that infrastructure dependency is resolved and the exact gate passes.

9. Correct overclaims: between 64.INIT load and init_load_banked, entry_main performs writes, including RAM-vector installation; they appear disjoint, so prove disjointness rather than claiming no writes. Preserve the vendor caveat that install ZP prerequisites may be incomplete (Krill README:182-184). Label 18-frame inter-call waits and 150-frame uninstall wait as repository empirical workarounds, not r194 API guarantees.

KRILL R194 HOST CONTRACT VERIFIED FOR THE REVISION

- install: KERNAL ROM enabled; input state must include valid FA and other KERNAL ZP whose upstream list is explicitly incomplete; output carry=status, A=status, X=drive type, Y=version-string ZP address on success; I is cleared. Evidence: tools/krill/loader/include/loader.inc:184-191 and README:172-184. Install may overwrite $0200-$03FF and may visibly render messages at $0400; README:178-181 and install.s:719-865.
- loadraw: X/Y points to a zero-terminated filename, first load uses the actual filename, carry set and A=status on error; X/Y and non-carry flags are not promised. With LOAD_TO_API=0 the PRG header controls destination. Evidence: loader.inc:196-212, README:192-214 and 230-234, c64/krill/loaderconfig.inc:23-29.
- uninstall: no inputs and all outputs undefined; evidence loader.inc:398-405. Reinitialize every relied-on register/flag/latch afterward.
- IRQ/NMI: Krill permits IRQ/NMI/DMA/sprites/badlines during transfer (README:51), but that does not make host RAM vectors safe. Install itself clears I. Host banking must keep the resident and CIA2 I/O visible during loadraw.
- memory/ZP: boot resident loadraw=$0400, uninstall=$04E1, resident $0400-$04ED; loader ZP $E0-$E4 is exclusive during active loads and reusable only while idle. Copy ZP $FB-$FE is disjoint. Evidence generated loadersymbols-c64.inc and README:236-240, 279-284.
- CIA/latches: while installed, $DD00 writes/restores must be values 0-3 with upper six bits zero and no unmasked RMW; CIA2 DDRA is loader-owned until uninstall. Evidence README:249-275 and src/hal/hal-c64-c128.inc.
- timing: no vendored post-install, inter-load, or post-uninstall delay is specified. The watchdog warning concerns starving an active loader for several frames (README:526-533). Existing 18/150-frame waits require local runtime evidence across enabled drive families.

APPROVAL STATUS

Revision 2 is not approved. The 64.INIT split and relocated display spans may remain as the basis of Revision 3, but implementation may proceed only after the design resolves items 1-5, corrects items 6-9, and supplies the revised executable verification plan. No product code was changed by this review.

# Design: Resume Krill after successful save-restore (C64)

Parent: moria8-x6t.2 (release-gating for the C64 fast-loader). Scope: C64 only.
This design refines the parent sketch with verified measurements and source
references. All addresses/sizes below are read from `build/c64/main.vs` and the
current sources on 2026-09-18.

## Revision history

- 2026-09-18 r1: initial design (moria8-mol-e5j).
- 2026-09-18 r2: rework per design review moria8-mol-wzv findings:
  - **moria8-mol-kcu.1**: `save_block_table_post_floor` is shared by
    `save_game` (save_write_block_table, save.s:720) and `load_game`
    (save.s:985). Retargeting its map descriptor to `MAP_STAGE_BASE` would
    make `save_game` serialize `$E000` overlay data instead of the live map.
    Fix: the save-side table is untouched; a C64-only load-side twin table
    carries the staged destination. See section 1.
  - **moria8-mol-kcu.2**: `overlay_invalidate` does not belong in shared
    save.s (cross-platform boundary; apple2/main.s:1645 imports the same
    file), and an invalidate placed in the load stream tail is coupled to
    load_game's internal control flow. Fix: invalidation moves to C64
    platform code in `title_load_game`, immediately after `jsr load_game`,
    covering success and all failure returns uniformly. See section 1b.

## Problem

After a successful title-screen restore, `title_load_game` jumps straight to
`load_resume_game` (c64/main.s:1076), bypassing `title_enter_menu` where the
only `krill_resume` call lives (c64/main.s:736-745). `krill_suspended` stays
`$ff` for the whole restored session, so every post-restore overlay and tier
load runs on stock KERNAL (~12-16 s per staircase vs ~1 s with Krill).

Why the obvious fix (call the existing `krill_resume` in `title_load_game`)
does not work, with evidence:

1. `load_game` streams the save record's map block directly into `MAP_BASE`
   `$C000` (platforms/shared/save.s:406 `save_block_desc(MAP_BASE, MAP_SIZE)`).
   `krill_resume` KERNAL-loads `kinst41` to `$C000` (main.s:2885-2899). After
   `load_game`, `$C000` holds the live restored map; installing there would
   destroy it.
2. `krill_resume` currently executes from ModalMiscOverlay at `$E447`
   (build/c64/main.vs: `.krill_resume $e447`, 104 B code + 7 B name). Its
   caller banks `$E000` RAM visible (`dec $01` at main.s:742). Any staging
   buffer at `$E000` therefore evicts the resume driver itself.

## Decision summary (unchanged from parent, now evidenced)

1. Stage the save record's map block at `$E000` (the 4 KB overlay window)
   instead of `$C000` during `load_game` only, behind a C64-only load-side
   descriptor table in platforms/shared/save.s. The save side keeps
   `MAP_BASE`. Save format unchanged: stream order and bytes are identical;
   only the load destination address changes.
2. Relocate the `krill_resume` driver from ModalMiscOverlay into resident
   Default-segment code so it can execute while `$E000` holds the staged map.
3. In `title_load_game`: after `jsr load_game`, invalidate the overlay window
   (C64 platform code); on success, after `disk_prompt_game_required` returns
   program media (main.s:1071-1072), call resident `krill_resume`, then copy
   the staged map `$E000` -> `$C000`, then `jmp load_resume_game`, whose
   `tier_restore_after_overlay` (core/game_loop.s:662) now dispatches through
   Krill.
4. Every failure mode clears Krill state and falls back to today's exact
   KERNAL path; the staged-map copy runs regardless of resume outcome.

## Verified facts the design rests on

Memory and segments:

- `MAP_BASE=$c000`, `MAP_END=$ceff`, 3840 B (c64/memory.s:28,153; MAP_SIZE =
  MAP_COLS*MAP_ROWS, core/dungeon_data.s:28,164). 3840 <= 4096, so the map
  fits the overlay window.
- Overlay/tier window: all overlay segments and `BANKED_DATA_BASE` share
  `$E000-$EFFF` (main.s:21-30, c64/memory.s:38). `tier_load` loads tier data
  over `$E000` and calls `overlay_invalidate` (core/tier_manager.s:265-273 and
  the tier_load prologue), so the staged map at `$E000` is dead immediately
  after the copy.
- Resident is 100% full: `.program_end = $c000` (main.vs). RuntimeBanked
  `$F000-$FFFA` is likewise committed (1 B class slack). Any resident growth
  requires byte recovery; the hard asserts stay untouched.
- ModalMiscOverlay is 3854/4096 B today (242 B free); removing `krill_resume`
  (~111 B) grows that slack but does not help the resident budget.
- kinst41.prg is 3214 B with PRG header `$C000`, spanning `$C000-$CC8D`, ending
  below `$D000`; the Makefile already asserts it loads wholly within
  `$C000-$CFFF` (platforms/commodore/Makefile:725-727). No third Krill build
  variant is introduced.

Code ownership (all from build/c64/main.vs):

- `load_game` $A351, `load_read_block` $A820, `load_read_block_table` $A510,
  `save_game`'s writer `save_write_block_table` (resident), `disk_prompt_game`
  $A9F4, `disk_prompt_game_required` $AD44, `overlay_invalidate` $4C44: all
  resident below `$C000`. The stream-read loop executes from resident RAM, so
  staging writes to `$E000` cannot clobber running code.
- `platforms/shared/save.s` is imported into the resident Default segment on
  C64 (main.s:600). The earlier c3r note placing save.s in ModalMiscOverlay
  is stale; current layout is resident.
- `save_block_table_post_floor` has exactly two users: `save_write_block_table`
  in `save_game` (save.s:720) and `load_read_block_table` in `load_game`
  (save.s:985). This dual use is why the staged destination must be a
  load-side-only table (review kcu.1).
- `load_read_block_table` always returns to its caller; stream errors set
  `save_io_error` and unwind through `load_read_block`'s loop exit, with the
  error branch taken by `load_game` after the table read returns
  (save.s:994-996). There is no direct jump from the reader into error
  handling, but the invalidate is nevertheless placed in the C64 caller
  (review kcu.2) so it is independent of load_game internals.
- C64 write-through: with `$01=$36` (KERNAL visible, used by the stream read)
  writes to `$E000-$FFFF` update the RAM under KERNAL. Reads of `$E000` in
  that banking return KERNAL ROM, so the staged copy must run with `$01=$34`
  or `$35` (HIRAM=0).
- Checksum (`save_cksum`) is accumulated from the read stream inside
  `load_read_byte`, independent of destination address (save.s load_read_block
  loop). Staging does not change checksum behavior.
- `load_game` has exactly one production caller on C64: `title_load_game`
  (main.s:1050).
- `krill_suspend` stays in ModalMiscOverlay: all four call sites already have
  ovl.modal loaded (main.s:1442-1445, 1755-1758, 2111-2114, and
  winner_royal_overlay at main.s:2927 inside the overlay itself).
- `disk_prompt_game`/`disk_prompt_game_required` are resident and load no
  overlay (disk_swap.s contains no `overlay_load`), so the staged map at
  `$E000` survives the post-load media prompts.
- `c64_disk_call`/`c64_disk_setnam`/`c64_disk_setlfs`/`c64_disk_close`/
  `c64_disk_clrchn` are resident trampolines that bank `$36` and `cli` around
  the KERNAL call themselves (main.s:276-337; static expectation at
  run_tests.sh:5025). A resident `krill_resume` therefore works from any
  caller banking with I/O visible; all runtime banking modes keep I/O visible.
- `krill_resume` self-gates: no-op when `krill_suspended` bit 7 clear; skips
  install when `krill_drive_1541` clear; on LOAD or install failure clears
  `krill_suspended` and leaves `krill_active=$00` (main.s:2866-2919). All of
  this logic is banking-neutral and relocates unchanged.
- C64 overlay dispatch is `HAL_PLATFORM_OVERLAY_SKIP_IF_CURRENT`
  (hal/lifecycle_policy.s:76): `overlay_load` trusts `current_overlay`. This
  creates the one new invariant below.

## Approach

### 1. Staged map destination: load-side twin table (platforms/shared/save.s)

The existing table is byte-identical on every platform and continues to serve
`save_game` on all targets and `load_game` on non-C64 targets:

```
save_block_table_post_floor:            // UNCHANGED: save_game + non-staged load
    :save_block_desc(recall_data_start, RECALL_DATA_SIZE)
#if !HAL_STORAGE_MAP_BANKED
    :save_block_desc(MAP_BASE, MAP_SIZE)
#endif
save_block_table_post_floor_end:
```

New C64-only flag (e.g. `HAL_STORAGE_MAP_RESTORE_STAGED`, defined in the C64
policy header next to `HAL_PLATFORM_OVERLAY_SKIP_IF_CURRENT`):

```
#if HAL_STORAGE_MAP_RESTORE_STAGED      // C64 only
// Load-side twin: identical stream order and sizes; the map block restores
// into the $E000 staging window instead of MAP_BASE. save_game never
// references this table, so save serialization is unaffected (kcu.1).
save_block_table_post_floor_load:
    :save_block_desc(recall_data_start, RECALL_DATA_SIZE)
    :save_block_desc(MAP_STAGE_BASE, MAP_SIZE)
save_block_table_post_floor_load_end:
.assert "load twin matches post-floor table shape", save_block_table_post_floor_load_end - save_block_table_post_floor_load, save_block_table_post_floor_end - save_block_table_post_floor
#endif
```

with `.const MAP_STAGE_BASE = $e000` in c64/memory.s and
`.assert "staged map fits overlay window", MAP_STAGE_BASE + MAP_SIZE <= $f000, true`.

At `load_game`'s post-floor read (save.s:985-990), select the twin under the
same flag; the count constant is shared (identical table shape, asserted):

```
#if HAL_STORAGE_MAP_RESTORE_STAGED
    lda #<save_block_table_post_floor_load
    sta zp_ptr1
    lda #>save_block_table_post_floor_load
    sta zp_ptr1_hi
#else
    lda #<save_block_table_post_floor   // existing lines unchanged
    sta zp_ptr1
    lda #>save_block_table_post_floor
    sta zp_ptr1_hi
#endif
    lda #SAVE_BLOCK_POST_FLOOR_COUNT
    jsr load_read_block_table
```

Cost: +8 B resident table; the call site is instruction-count neutral (same
4 instructions, different label). C128 is already excluded from this table by
`HAL_STORAGE_MAP_BANKED` (save.s:405-407,991-993) and is untouched; Plus/4
and Apple IIe keep the `#else` branch byte-identical.

Staging is unconditional on C64: descriptor tables are static data and a
conditional destination would need a runtime hook in `load_read_block_table`.
The copy costs ~80 ms once per restore (3840 B, ~20 cycles/B), invisible next
to disk I/O, and buys a single uniform path for Krill and KERNAL sessions.

### 1b. Overlay invalidation in C64 platform code (title_load_game)

New invariant: staging silently clobbers the `$E000` image while
`current_overlay` may still name OVL_MODAL_MISC from the slot prompt
(main.s:1442). Under SKIP_IF_CURRENT, a later `overlay_load(OVL_MODAL_MISC)`
would skip the disk load and execute staged map bytes as code.

Placement (c64/main.s, `title_load_game`):

```
    jsr load_game
    jsr overlay_invalidate        // NEW: staged map may have clobbered $E000
    bcc !title_load_fail+         // existing
```

- Platform code, not shared save.s: the hazard is a C64 artifact of
  MAP_STAGE_BASE, and shared save.s is compiled by non-Commodore targets
  (apple2/main.s:1645) whose overlay machinery differs (kcu.2).
- Immediately after `jsr load_game`, before the carry branch: covers success
  and every failure return. `load_game` fails closed (`clc; rts`) on all
  error paths, so this single site dominates them all, independent of
  load_game's internal control flow (kcu.2).
- Unconditional: on early failures nothing was staged, and invalidation only
  forces the next title overlay load to refetch from disk - safe and rare.
- `overlay_invalidate` is resident ($4C44), so no banking dance is needed.

### 2. Relocate `krill_resume` to resident Default segment

Move `krill_resume`, `krill_resume_name`, and its door-scan scratch assert
(main.s:2866-2924) from `.segment ModalMiscOverlay` to `.segment Default`,
code unchanged. ~111 B resident cost, ~111 B freed in ovl.modal.

Relocation is forced, not optional: the staged map occupies `$E000` from
inside `load_game` until after `krill_resume` runs, and reloading ovl.modal
before resume would overwrite the staged map (the only copy). kinst41 cannot
move to `$E000` either (staged map there; parent excludes a third build
variant; link constraint is `$C000` span ending below `$D000`).

Simplify the existing `title_enter_menu` resume block (main.s:736-745): with
the driver resident, drop the `lda #OVL_MODAL_MISC / jsr overlay_load / bcs /
sei / dec $01` prologue (~13 B recovered in resident). Keep
`jsr krill_resume` followed by `jsr platform_runtime_resync_c64`, preserving
today's post-state exactly. This also removes the stale-skip hazard on the
save-quit/death return path.

`krill_suspend` remains in ModalMiscOverlay; it is only ever needed before
KERNAL stream I/O with ovl.modal already resident, and it never runs while
`$E000` holds a staged map.

### 3. `title_load_game` success path (c64/main.s:1071-1076)

```
    jsr disk_prompt_game            // existing
    jsr disk_prompt_game_required   // existing: program media back in drive
    jsr krill_resume                // NEW: resident, self-gated on krill_suspended
    jsr map_stage_copy              // NEW: $E000 -> $C000, MAP_SIZE bytes
    jmp load_resume_game            // existing
```

No `platform_runtime_resync_c64` at this site: today's entry state to
`load_resume_game` (post-`disk_prompt_game_required`) is preserved bit-for-bit.
`krill_resume`'s KERNAL calls self-bank through the `c64_disk_*` trampolines;
its 18-frame raster settle only needs I/O visible, which every runtime banking
mode satisfies.

`map_stage_copy` is new resident code, self-contained: save `$01`, `sei`,
select `$35` (HIRAM=0 so `$E000` RAM reads back), copy 15 pages (3840 B),
restore `$01` and flags. ~35-40 B. It must not depend on `$E000`/`$C000`
content as code and must run unconditionally on the success path (staging was
unconditional).

Order is mandated: `krill_resume` first (it clobbers `$C000-$CC8D` via
kinst41), copy second (restores the map over whatever resume left), regardless
of resume success/failure.

### 4. Byte budget

Resident Default growth: ~111 B (krill_resume + name) + ~38 B
(map_stage_copy) + 6 B (krill_resume/map_stage_copy jsr sites) + 3 B
(overlay_invalidate jsr) + 8 B (load-side twin table) - ~13 B
(title_enter_menu simplification) = ~153 B net recovery required below
`$C000`.

Precedent exists (2feedd7 recovered 255 B via helper dedup; c3r recovered
~20 B). Recovery must come from code structure/dedup only - never from
player-visible text or boundary asserts (AGENTS.md non-negotiables). If
recovery cannot reach ~153 B, stop and report; do not weaken
`program_end <= $C000`.

## Invariants

1. `program_end <= $C000`; RuntimeBanked `$F000-$FFFA`; overlay window
   `$E000-$EFFF`; kinst41 span `$C000-$CFFF` (Makefile:727). All existing
   asserts stay; add `MAP_STAGE_BASE + MAP_SIZE <= $F000` and the twin-table
   shape assert from section 1.
2. Save format byte-identical: same blocks, same order, same checksum
   coverage. `save_game` keeps reading the live map from `MAP_BASE` through
   the untouched `save_block_table_post_floor` (kcu.1). Round-trip
   save/restore produces an identical map at `$C000`.
3. Staged map copy runs on every `load_game` success path, independent of
   Krill state; `krill_resume` is the only Krill-gated step.
4. `overlay_invalidate` executes in `title_load_game` on every `load_game`
   return, before any subsequent `overlay_load` can consult `current_overlay`
   (SKIP_IF_CURRENT platform) (kcu.2).
5. No KERNAL IEC transaction while `krill_active=$ff` (settled c3r/c3r.2
   rule): the restore flow is already inside the suspend window opened by
   `save_prepare_slot_prompt` (main.s:1041,1445); `krill_resume` only runs
   while suspended.
6. KERNAL fallback sessions (`krill_suspended=$00`) behave exactly as today
   plus one ~80 ms copy; no Krill file is touched.
7. No player-visible string changes; no new strings required (resume failure
   degrades silently, as today).

## Failure modes and required behavior

- kinst41 LOAD fails (wrong/missing disk in program drive): existing
  `krill_resume` fallback clears `krill_suspended`, `krill_active` stays `$00`;
  copy still runs; session continues on KERNAL exactly like today's restored
  sessions. (Pattern already proven by resume_missing_kinst41_product_smoke.)
- Installer `jsr $c000` returns carry set: same fallback. `$C000` holds
  installer garbage until the copy restores the map - order mandated above.
- Non-1541-family drive (`krill_drive_1541=$00`): no install attempt; KERNAL
  continues (documented 1581 limitation from moria8-c3r).
- Krill never installed this session (`krill_suspended=$00`, incl.
  BYPASS_SLOT_PROMPT test paths where `save_prepare_slot_prompt` is skipped):
  `krill_resume` no-ops; copy runs; behavior identical to today.
- Corrupt/short save detected after the map block staged: no copy; map `$C000`
  retains pre-load (dead, title-owned) content instead of today's partial
  overwrite. Not player-visible: `$C000` is rewritten by generation or the
  next load before any use. `current_overlay` is already invalidated by the
  platform-code invalidate, so the title path cannot execute stale `$E000`
  bytes regardless of where the stream failed.
- `load_game` failure before the map block: identical to today (plus the
  harmless invalidation).
- Single-drive swap: `disk_prompt_save` / `disk_prompt_game` choreography
  unchanged; kinst41 is read after program media is verified back.
- REU systems: orthogonal. Resume attempt runs identically; post-restore
  overlay/tier reads hit the REU stash first, Krill on miss.
- Second drive (save disk on device 9): suspend already covers the shared-ATN
  rule (drivecode1541.s:906-914 auto-uninstall); kinst41 loads from
  `program_device` only.

## Third-party contract status

No new external surface: reuse of kinst41/install under the host-environment
contract already established and reviewed in moria8-mol-ayy / moria8-c3r
(tools/krill/loader README, include/loader.inc:184-236,398-406;
docs/Protocol.txt:39-77). Items binding this design: install requires KERNAL
visible and returns carry/A/X/Y per loader.inc:184-194 (the `c64_disk_call`
trampoline supplies `$36`+cli); runtime raw loads need the resident at `$F000`
and I/O visible; every `$DD00` restore writes `$00-$03` only; loader ZP
`$E0-$E4` untouched while loads are active. The map copy and staging touch no
Krill state.

## Tests and verification

New/updated evidence:

1. New scripted product smoke (TDE drive): boot with Krill, restore an
   existing save through the production `title_load_game` path; assert
   `krill_active=$ff`, `krill_suspended=$00`, `krill_boot_used=$01` at
   `c64_test_after_load_resume_game`; monitor breakpoint on `KRILL_LOAD_FILE`
   proves the post-restore tier load dispatched through Krill.
2. Extend the missing-kinst41 pattern to the restore flow: restore with
   kinst41 absent completes on KERNAL (`krill_active=$00`,
   `krill_suspended=$00`), session reaches main loop, a subsequent overlay
   load succeeds via KERNAL.
3. Existing round-trip smokes (save_write, load_resume,
   single_drive_load_return) pass unchanged - they are the
   restored-map-renders-identically gate and the save-side regression for
   kcu.1 (save_game still serializes from MAP_BASE); add krill state
   assertions to the single-drive load smoke to cover swap choreography.
4. chest_open_product_reu_smoke stays green (REU parity).
5. Static: `make build` (program_end, overlay window, new staged-window and
   twin-table asserts, kinst41 span via Makefile), `make check-hal-boundaries`
   (shared save.s load-side table).
6. Gate: `make test64` in full before feature completion (parent acceptance).

## Architectural change record

Problem and success criteria: restored sessions run entirely on KERNAL today;
success is post-restore tier/overlay loads dispatching through Krill with the
evidence above and `make test64` green.
State being changed: map-restore destination on the load side only (transient
staging at `$E000`), `krill_resume` code home (overlay -> resident),
`current_overlay` validity across every `load_game` return, krill lifecycle
state across the restore transition.
Search scope and terms: `load_game`, `save_game`, `save_block_desc(MAP_BASE`,
`save_block_table_post_floor`, `save_write_block_table`,
`load_read_block*`, `title_load_game`, `krill_resume`, `krill_suspend`,
`overlay_invalidate`, `current_overlay`, `tier_restore_after_overlay`,
`MAP_BASE`, `BANKED_DATA_BASE`, `kinst41`, `$E000` ownership.
Relevant readers/writers and exclusions: C64 restore path only; save-side
table explicitly untouched. C128 (HAL_STORAGE_MAP_BANKED), Plus/4, Apple IIe
excluded by flag gating; their descriptor lines and control flow are
byte-identical.
Initialization/reset/persistence: staging is per-restore transient; krill
state bytes remain session-local at `$0336-$033B`; nothing enters the save
format.
Affected sequence: slot prompt (suspend) -> stream read with map staged at
`$E000` (load-side twin table) -> title_load_game invalidates overlay state
on any return -> on success, program media restored -> krill_resume (kinst41
-> `$C000`, install, settle) -> map copy `$E000`->`$C000` ->
load_resume_game (tier/overlay via Krill).
Contract authority: AGENTS.md hard boundaries; vendored Krill contract cited
above; TURN_RENDER_CONTRACT loaded - no event-lifetime, visibility-producer,
renderer, or repeat-command rows apply (restore recomputes visibility through
the unchanged `load_resume_game` path; render identity is gated by unchanged
round-trip smokes). MONSTER_STATE and DUNGEON_GENERATION contracts not
matched. Tier: Architectural (loader + memory ownership + lifecycle).
Intentional deviations: staged map destination on C64 load side only; failed
loads no longer partially overwrite `$C000` (not observable).
Widths/carry/range: 16-bit block addresses/sizes; `MAP_SIZE=3840 <= 4096`
asserted; twin-table shape asserted equal to the save table; carry semantics
of `load_game`/`krill_resume` unchanged; copy length is a build-time constant.
RNG: N/A - no RNG reads or writes on this path.
Affected platforms/overlays/banks/owners: C64 only; resident Default (growth
~153 B, recovery required), ModalMiscOverlay (-111 B), `$E000` window gains a
transient staging role during restore, `$C000` map ownership unchanged after
the copy.
Required production-path tests: items 1-6 above.
Out of scope: other platforms, save-format changes, compression/packing,
write acceleration, directory reorder (moria8-0dn), UX changes.
Unresolved uncertainty and risk: the ~153 B resident byte-recovery source is
implementation work with precedent; if it cannot be found without touching
text or asserts, stop and report. No user-facing or layout decision remains
open; the parent bead already settled staging, relocation, and ordering.

## Open questions

None blocking. All layout/behavior choices were pre-decided in moria8-x6t.2
and confirmed against current sources above; review findings kcu.1 and kcu.2
are incorporated in r2. The byte-recovery target is an implementation
constraint, not a design fork.

All claims verified against build/c64/main.vs and current sources. Ready for review (moria8-mol-wzv).

design:
# Design: C64 fast-loader for all read stages

## Decision and scope

Use Krill r194 as the C64 program-media PRG loader from boot through gameplay. Keep one raw-load resident at `$F000`; after successful boot installation, keep the drive-side loader installed and route title art, tier data, on-demand overlays, and REU preload reads through the existing `hal_asset_load_prg_header` boundary. Preserve stock KERNAL behavior as the complete fallback when installation or later reinstallation fails.

In this design, all read stages means all read-only program-media PRG assets:

1. Boot chain: `MORIA64` and `64.BANK`.
2. Title: `T64`.
3. Creature tiers: `MONSTER.DB.1` through `MONSTER.DB.4`.
4. Overlays: `64.START`, `64.TOWN`, `64.DEATH`, `64.GEN`, `64.HELP`, `64.UI`, `64.ITEMS`, `64.SPELL`, `64.MODAL`, and `64.CHEST`.
5. REU preload: the same tier and overlay assets through the same HAL dispatch.

Excluded from Krill raw loading are record streams and DOS operations: saved-game reads and writes, high-score reads and writes, marker reads and writes, command-channel status, drive probes/init, and save-file existence checks. Those paths require `OPEN`/`CHKIN`/`CHRIN`/`CHKOUT`/`CHROUT` semantics and remain stock KERNAL operations inside a Krill suspension window. Boot art and loader installer/resident bootstrap files also remain KERNAL-loaded because Krill is not installed yet.

No file packing, compression, random access, or Krill save plugin is introduced. Those change formats, memory ownership, and tooling and require separate design work.

## Existing architecture to preserve

- `overlay_load_disk` and `tier_load_disk` already converge on `hal_asset_load_prg_header` (`platforms/commodore/common/overlay.s:257-321`, `core/tier_manager.s:617-636`).
- Title loading uses the same PRG-header destination path through `hal_asset_load_title` (`platforms/commodore/c64/config.s:185-193`).
- C64 filenames are platform-owned, counted for KERNAL, and zero-terminated for Krill (`platforms/commodore/c64/hal/storage.s:150-224`, `hal/storage_title_name.s:1-9`). Common gameplay code must not learn Krill or C64 filenames.
- The runtime resident is linked first in `RuntimeBanked` at `$F000`; `$F000-$FFFA` remains the hard payload window (`platforms/commodore/c64/main.s:31-68`, `2678-2706`).
- Overlay and tier data continue to share `$E000-$EFFF`; existing invalidation, REU, and fallback behavior remains authoritative (`platforms/commodore/common/overlay.s:1-7`, `core/tier_manager.s:274-433`).

## State machine and flow

Use explicit state bytes in always-visible RAM:

- `krill_active=$ff`: host resident and drive code are synchronized; program assets may use Krill.
- `krill_active=$00, krill_suspended=$ff`: drive code was intentionally uninstalled for KERNAL IEC work; resume may be attempted only in safe title context.
- `krill_active=$00, krill_suspended=$00`: permanent KERNAL fallback for the current session.
- `krill_boot_used!=0`: evidence only that the boot chain used Krill; never use it as dispatch state.

Boot sequence:

1. KERNAL-load and execute the full installer with KERNAL visible.
2. Record compatible drive family and set handoff magic only after successful installation and drive settle.
3. Krill-load `MORIA64`, then `64.BANK`, preserving filenames in the copied low-memory chain stub because `MORIA64` overwrites the original boot image.
4. On either raw-load failure, uninstall, clear handoff state, wait for stock DOS recovery, and retry the normal KERNAL chain.
5. Main startup adopts handoff state. Successful handoff sets `krill_active=$ff`; direct start, missing loader files, incompatible devices, and failed install leave `$00`.

Program asset sequence:

1. Callers pass counted length plus X/Y filename to `hal_asset_load_prg_header`.
2. If `krill_active` is negative, dispatch to the raw loader using the zero terminator already present after every C64 asset name.
3. Otherwise execute the existing KERNAL `SETNAM`/`SETLFS`/`LOAD`/`CLOSE`/`CLRCHN` path.
4. Preserve carry as the public success result and preserve Krill status in A on the fast path. Restore caller banking and the legal CIA2/VIC state before returning.
5. Existing caller behavior remains unchanged: title text fallback, tier invalidation/embedded fallback, and overlay load failure all continue to branch on carry.

KERNAL IEC sequence:

1. Before any KERNAL IEC transaction on any device, load the modal helper while Krill is still active, then call `krill_suspend`.
2. Uninstall deliberately and wait for stock DOS to become ready before issuing KERNAL traffic.
3. Run the entire stream/probe/status transaction under KERNAL ownership. Do not alternate KERNAL and Krill calls within one transaction.
4. At title re-entry, and only while the map window is not live, load the compact 1541-family installer to `$C000`, execute it, settle, and restore `krill_active=$ff`.
5. If compact-installer load or install fails, clear suspended state and continue under KERNAL. Reinstallation failure is nonfatal and must never leave host state claiming that Krill is active.

The suspend rule has no device-number exception. IEC ATN is shared. The 1541 drive idle loop branches to uninstall when ATN is asserted (`tools/krill/loader/src/drives/drivecode1541.s:906-914`). A KERNAL operation directed to device 9 can therefore uninstall drive 8. Missing a suspension boundary creates host/drive state divergence and a later `pollblock` hang.

## Third-party host contract

Interface documentation was read end-to-end: `tools/krill/loader/README`, `docs/Prerequisites.txt`, `docs/Protocol.txt`, and `include/loader.inc`.

Registers and flags:

- Install returns carry set on error, A=status, X=drive type, Y=version-pointer ZP address (`include/loader.inc:184-194`). The install implementation calls KERNAL services, so no other register or flag preservation is assumed.
- `loadraw` takes X/Y as the low/high pointer to a zero-terminated filename and returns carry set on error with A=status (`README:189-214`, `include/loader.inc:196-236`, `src/resident.s:240-282`). X, Y, all undocumented flags, and loader ZP are caller-clobbered unless explicitly restored by Moria8.
- `uninstall` has no input and undefined output (`include/loader.inc:398-406`, `src/resident.s:1343-1353`). Callers preserve anything needed across it.

Required host and latch state:

- Install runs with KERNAL ROM enabled; it invokes KERNAL routines and may clear I through those routines (`README:162-187`, `include/loader.inc:184-191`). Moria8 sets the intended boot device in the active-drive variable before install; installer source probes that device first and leaves the selected active device in FA (`src/install.s:210-280`).
- Runtime raw loads require the resident bytes visible at `$F000` and C64 I/O visible at `$D000-$DFFF`; Moria8 therefore calls with `$01=$35`, never all-RAM configurations that hide CIA2.
- After installation, every write restoring `$DD00` must be in `$00-$03`; upper six bits must remain zero (`README:249-275`). Moria8 uses `$03` for VIC bank 0 and released IEC lines. No read-modify-write restore is allowed.
- Krill owns CIA2 serial direction/latches while active. The HAL defines installed/idle protocol states via `$DD02` and switches to KERNAL mode during uninstall (`src/hal/hal-c64-c128.inc:236-281`, `391-429`, `602-605`; `src/hal/hal.inc:12-19`). Standard KERNAL IEC calls are forbidden while host state is active.
- Filename storage must remain visible for the call and be zero-terminated. Wildcards are unsupported (`README:189-216`).

Interrupt tolerance and timing:

- The loader documents IRQ, NMI, DMA, sprites, and badlines as unrestricted and describes itself as inert while idle (`README:44-64`, `236-240`). Moria8 may leave runtime text-mode IRQs enabled, provided interrupt handlers obey the CIA2 and loader-ZP contracts. Boot-time screen blanking remains a conservative current behavior and is not broadened into a new runtime requirement by this design.
- Loader ZP is `$E0-$E4` in the configured C64 build (`tools/krill/loader/build/loadersymbols-c64.inc:33-37`) and must not be written while a load is active (`README:279-284`). Existing game caller-save discipline must cover these bytes.
- No fixed completion time is assumed. The protocol polls drive readiness (`docs/Protocol.txt:39-77`). Installation and back-to-back transfers need explicit readiness/settle handling proven by production smokes; do not replace them with emulator-specific short cycle spins.
- The drive watchdog can reset after protocol starvation; default watchdog behavior remains enabled (`include/loader.inc:5-8`). Runtime verification therefore treats hangs/timeouts as protocol failures, not nondeterministic emulator behavior.

## Memory and ownership

- Preserve the C64 resident boundary `program_end <= $C000`, map ownership `$C000-$CEFF`, floor items `$CF00-$CFFF`, every overlay `$E000-$EFFF`, and runtime banked payload ending at or below `$FFFA`. Never weaken these assertions.
- Keep the 238-byte raw+uninstall resident pinned at `$F000` and assert entry offsets against generated artifacts.
- Suspend/resume code belongs in `OVL_MODAL_MISC`, not default resident or the nearly full runtime bank. It is needed by title/save/death lifecycle paths and is loaded before invoking KERNAL streams.
- The compact 1541-family installer uses title-owned `$C000-$CFFF` only when no live dungeon map exists. Assert its PRG header is `$C000` and its complete span ends below `$D000`; never install over a live map.
- State bytes remain below `$033C`, outside the cassette-buffer/door-scan scratch window, with an assertion.
- New filenames must be included in the Krill 16-bit hash collision check because hash collisions can silently select the wrong file (`README:503-520`; `tools/check_krill_filenames.py`). Directory construction must retain at least two entries and a valid final directory block.

## Failure modes and required behavior

- Missing/incompatible initial loader: remain on KERNAL and reach normal title/gameplay.
- Boot raw-load failure: uninstall, wait for DOS recovery, clear handoff, and KERNAL-retry without reading filenames from overwritten boot memory.
- Missing program asset under Krill: return carry set and status A; existing title/tier/overlay error behavior applies.
- KERNAL call while active: prohibited by design because ATN can auto-uninstall drive code and leave stale host state.
- Missing/wrong disk during resume: clear suspended state, keep `krill_active=$00`, and continue safely under KERNAL.
- Non-1541-family resume: do not run the compact installer; remain on KERNAL. Initial full installer detection and fallback remain unchanged.
- Save/high-score/marker failure: preserve current diagnostics and player-visible strings. Fast loading must not weaken save integrity checks or status classification.
- Illegal `$DD00` value, hidden I/O, overwritten `$E0-$E4`, installer/map overlap, or stale active state: memory/protocol defect, never paper over it with longer timeouts.
- Release attribution: official release media/archive must include the required binary attribution, such as `Loader by Krill`, because the vendored license requires attribution in the production or accompanying official material (`tools/krill/loader/README:545-568`). Existing `LICENSE` and `SOURCE-OFFER` shipping requirements remain unchanged.

## Verification and acceptance

Focused iteration may use individual C64 product smokes, but final implementation gate is `make test64` under the repository 30-second-per-command policy.

Required evidence:

1. Fastload product smoke proves Krill boot handoff, title load, and a post-title asset dispatch hit `krill_load_file`, with `krill_active=$ff` and `krill_boot_used!=0`.
2. Missing-installer/incompatible-device smoke proves `krill_active=$00`, `krill_boot_used=$00`, and normal KERNAL title path.
3. Non-REU gameplay smoke executes real overlay and tier production dispatches through Krill.
4. REU smoke proves preload reads use Krill and later gameplay uses the REU without corrupting loader state.
5. Dual-drive save smoke suspends before device-9 KERNAL traffic, saves successfully, resumes on device 8, then performs a real Krill overlay read.
6. Missing/wrong `KINST41` resume smoke proves graceful permanent KERNAL fallback with no hang.
7. One-drive disk-swap, load-record, save-record, high-score/death, retirement, and Disk Setup smokes remain green.
8. Static/build checks prove program, overlay, runtime-bank, chain-stub, compact-installer, state-byte, PRG-header, and filename-hash boundaries.
9. Disk/image inspection proves loader attribution plus required `license,s` and `source-offer,s` files are present.
10. Review the final diff to ensure no player-visible text or boundary assertion was weakened and no generated artifact was left in source directories.

## Architectural change record

Problem and success criteria: C64 program assets remain fast-loaded after boot without breaking KERNAL stream I/O, media swaps, fallback devices, memory ownership, or save integrity. Success is the evidence and full gate above.
State being changed: loader lifecycle state only: active, suspended for KERNAL, or permanent fallback.
Search scope and terms: boot `LOAD`, `hal_asset_load*`, overlay/tier/title loads, REU preload, storage HAL, save/load streams, marker, high score, Disk Setup, Krill install/loadraw/uninstall, CIA2, `$01`, `$DD00`, `$DD02`, and ZP `$E0-$E4`.
Relevant readers/writers and exclusions: C64 boot, config, main lifecycle trampolines, shared overlay/tier readers, REU preload, storage and save flows. C128, Plus/4, Apple IIe, writes, packing, and compression are excluded.
Initialization/reset/persistence: initialize from boot handoff in `init_load_banked`; reset to KERNAL on direct start/install failure; suspend before any KERNAL IEC transaction; resume only at title; state is session-local and not saved.
Affected sequence: boot install -> main/bank raw loads -> title/tier/overlay/REU raw loads -> suspend -> KERNAL stream or DOS operation -> title-safe compact reinstall or permanent fallback.
Contract authority: C64 memory assertions and storage HAL ownership, then vendored Krill r194 README/interface/source references above. Prior accepted project decision is recorded in `moria8-c3r`.
Intentional deviations: raw program assets only; no Krill save plugin, compression, packing, or native resume for non-1541-family drives.
Widths/carry/range: 16-bit filename pointers; zero-terminated names up to 16 chars; carry clear success/set failure; A preserves 8-bit Krill status; installer and payload spans are assertion-guarded.
RNG: N/A; loader does not read or change gameplay RNG.
Affected platform/banks/owners: C64 only; low handoff/state RAM, `$C000` title-time installer window, `$E000` modal helper, `$F000` runtime resident, CIA2 IEC/VIC latches, and loader ZP `$E0-$E4`.
Required production tests: items 1-9 above.
Out of scope: other platforms, write acceleration, new UX, file-format changes, decompression, packed phase blobs, and directory-order performance optimization.
Unresolved uncertainty and risk: no design-blocking questions remain because `moria8-c3r` records accepted choices for title conversion, suspend/resume, non-1541 fallback, and deferring packing/compression. Implementation review must still verify every KERNAL IEC entry point is dominated by suspension and that official release attribution is actually present.

1. REJECTED DECISION: Second-drive KERNAL I/O without Krill suspend (Design Section 2)

Place krill_suspend and krill_resume in ModalMiscOverlay. For hal_asset_load_title, any resident dispatch growth must be offset by recovering equivalent bytes in resident.

- In hal_asset_krill_call, preserve return status in A alongside carry across the banking restore.

design:
# Design: Krill for all read loads (C64)

Scope: C64 only. Keep the Krill resident installed for the whole session so every
read load dispatches through the existing `hal_asset_krill_call` path
(config.s:131). Stream I/O (saves, restore, hall of fame, save-disk marker)
stays on the stock KERNAL inside temporary uninstall windows. No decompression,
no file packing in this feature (RuntimeBanked is full; both are follow-ups).

## Measured facts (evidence for decisions)

- RuntimeBanked segment: `$F000-$FFF5` used of `$F000-$FFF6` window — **1 byte free**.
  No decompressor (~200-400 B) or save plugin can live there without separate
  budget-recovery work.
- Map area: `$C000-$CEFF` (3840 B, memory.s:28), dead at title (no game started
  or between games), live during gameplay.
- kinst64 (full drive-detect installer): 6998 B — fits nowhere at runtime.
- **1541-only installer (ONLY_1541_AND_COMPATIBLE=1): 3226 B** — fits the dead
  map area at title. Installer segment must end below `$D000` (link-time
  constraint, verified) — `$C000+$CC9A` qualifies; `$E000` window does not.
- Krill save plugin: rejected without full measurement — it embeds save
  drivecode (>1 KB host code) plus needs a $0800-byte scratch buffer
  (samples/save/save.s:31), and our save flow (platforms/shared/save.s,
  2580 lines: overwrite probe, save-media swap prompts, wrong-media detection,
  stream status) is deeply stream/KERNAL-shaped. Rebuilding that UX against the
  whole-buffer plugin API is out of proportion vs. the suspend/resume below.
- Tier files are tiny (832-2064 B); overlays ~4 KB; title 622 B.
- Screen-blank requirement (docs/krill_fuckup.md:19,58): SENDBYTE is
  cycle-timed; **multicolor bitmap mode** badlines break it. Text mode is
  listed as a safe condition. So: keep blanking for the boot bitmap phase;
  gameplay text-mode loads run screen-on (verified by the runtime suite; any
  regression hangs a smoke decisively via watchdog timeout).

## Decisions

### 1. Loads that convert
- Already converted (dispatch exists, just stays active): overlays, tier DBs,
  REU preload set.
- Convert: title art — add the `bit krill_active / bmi` dispatch to
  `hal_asset_load_title` (config.s:186), same pattern as
  `hal_asset_load_prg_header`. Observable change: the brief KERNAL
  "SEARCHING FOR T64" output disappears (load becomes near-instant).
- Not converted (stream I/O, stays KERNAL inside suspend windows): save write,
  restore/read, hall of fame (HALL.OF.FAME), MORIA8.ID marker, save-file
  probes. Save-file parsing is stream-shaped and save files may live on a
  foreign save disk.

### 2. Saves: suspend/resume, not the save plugin
- `krill_suspend`: before **any KERNAL IEC transaction on ANY device** — dummy
  reload of a known-present file (busy-window contract, proven in
  krill_boot_finish), `KRILL_RUNTIME_UNINSTALL`, ~0.33 s settle.
  **REVIEW CORRECTION (c3r.2, verified in drivecode1541.s:906-914):** the IEC
  ATN line is shared across all devices; drive 8's `idleloop41` polls ATN IN
  and auto-uninstalls to stock DOS on ANY bus activity (`bpl uninstall`). A
  KERNAL transaction to a second drive therefore silently uninstalls drive 8
  while krill_active=$ff, and the next Krill read hangs permanently in
  pollblock. There is no "other device" exemption.
  - Corollary (implementation checklist): audit ALL KERNAL I/O call sites
    (save.s, disk_swap.s, save_slot_menu.s, HALL.OF.FAME, MORIA8.ID marker,
    save-file probes, media-status reads) — any path missed by the suspend
    wrapper is a hang, not a degradation.
- `krill_resume`: after the flow completes — reload the 1541-only installer
  (`kinst41`, new build artifact, 3226 B) to `$C000` and run it. Only legal
  where the map is dead: **title context**. Drive-type gate: record at boot
  whether the drive is 1541-compatible (`$0339`); resume only then.
  - 1571: works via 1541 compatibility (loses 1571 native speed after resume —
    acceptable).
  - 1581/FD/other: resume skipped, session continues on KERNAL (today's
    behavior; 1581 KERNAL is tolerable). Documented limitation.
- Resume failure (e.g. kinst41 not on the disk currently inserted):
  krill_active stays $00, game continues exactly like today's KERNAL fallback;
  retry on the next suspend exit. Never fatal.
- Assumption to verify in implementation: all save flows are session-ending or
  title-context (Moria saves at death/retirement/save+quit). If a
  save-and-continue flow exists, that session degrades to KERNAL until return
  to title (map is live; `$C000` unavailable). Flagged as open question.

### 3. Packing / staging buffer
Deferred (follow-up bead). Per-file loads stay. The directory-order reorder
(moria8-0dn) is independent and still worthwhile.

### 4. Decompressor
Deferred (follow-up bead). RuntimeBanked has 1 free byte; enabling LZSA2/ZX0
needs budget recovery plus build-tooling changes. Not part of this feature.

### 5. KERNAL fallback parity
Untouched. krill_active=$00 path (no magic / failed install / incompatible
drive / failed resume) is byte-identical behavior to today. Boot-time full
installer (6998 B, all drive types) unchanged — 1541-only installer is used
only for runtime resume.

### 6. Error UX
Krill status codes (config.s:124-129) map to carry-set semantics in
`hal_asset_krill_call`; existing carry-set handling (tier embedded fallback,
overlay skip, title fail) applies unchanged. Suspend/resume failures degrade
silently to KERNAL. No new player-visible strings required.
- REVIEW ADDITION (c3r.2): preserve the Krill status byte in A across the
  banking restore in both `krill_load_file` and `hal_asset_krill_call`
  (currently destroyed — A returns $03/flags). ~4-6 B; folds into the byte
  recovery below.

### 7. Memory budget
- New flag bytes in the `$0334-$033B` always-RAM gap (config.s:106 asserts
  below `$033C`): `krill_suspended = $0338`, `krill_drive_1541 = $0339`.
- krill_active semantics: `$ff` = installed/active (now the steady state),
  `$00` = not installed (fallback or suspended). `$55` marker **removed** —
  krill_boot_finish's uninstall ceremony is deleted; boot gets faster and
  quieter (no dummy reload, settle, DOS reboot at startup). `krill_boot_used`
  ($0337) unchanged as smoke evidence.
- New artifact: `kinst41.prg` (3226 B, INSTALL=$C000,
  ONLY_1541_AND_COMPATIBLE=1) added to the disk + REU/fastload smoke disks.
  Disk cost: ~13 blocks. Boot installer unchanged.
- REVIEW CORRECTION (c3r.2, verified): resident below `$C000` is 100% full
  (program_end=$C000) and RuntimeBanked has 1 free byte — suspend/resume code
  CANNOT go resident. Home `krill_suspend`/`krill_resume` in
  **ModalMiscOverlay** ($E000-$EE63 = 3684/4096 B, 412 B free), which already
  hosts save.s, disk_swap.s, title_screen.s, save_slot_menu.s (main.s:596-598,
  2853) and is therefore loaded at exactly the title/save contexts where
  suspend/resume run. The `hal_asset_load_title` dispatch and status-in-A
  preservation grow resident config.s/RuntimeBanked by ~20 B total and must be
  offset by equivalent byte recovery (precedent: the 255 B core/ recovery).

### 8. Test / evidence plan
- fastload_product_smoke: expect `krill_active=$ff` (was `$55`).
- fallback smoke: unchanged ($00/$00).
- chest_open_product_reu_smoke: `$55` -> `$ff`.
- New evidence: test-define counter incremented in `hal_asset_krill_call`,
  asserted >0 after a scripted post-title overlay swap (proves gameplay-time
  loads dispatch through Krill).
- Save smokes (scripted save write product suite): must pass unchanged —
  they are the suspend/resume regression. Add expectation `krill_active=$ff`
  after save completes (proves resume).
- Screen-on text-mode loading: implicitly covered by every runtime smoke once
  blanking is dropped for text-mode loads; a hang is a hard failure.
- REVIEW ADDITIONS (c3r.2) — new required tests:
  (a) save to a second drive (-9 save disk) followed by a drive-8 overlay
      read — exercises the ATN auto-uninstall hang from section 2;
  (b) disk-swap / resume failure: wrong disk left in drive 8 at resume,
      session must degrade to KERNAL and keep working;
  (c) title art Krill dispatch evidence.
- Gate: `make test64` (full suite) before feature completion, plus targeted
  iteration on the smokes above.
- Implementation must follow AGENTS.md Behavior Change Protocol: load
  docs/TURN_RENDER_CONTRACT.md if display/blanking behavior changes; no player
  text changes; boundary asserts stay.

## Open questions — RESOLVED (user, this session)
1. Save-and-continue: accepted — all saves treated as session-ending or
   title-context; any missed flow degrades to KERNAL until title.
2. 1581/non-1541-compatible drives: accepted — KERNAL after first save of a
   session (user notes 1581 KERNAL is fast on its own, which is correct).
3. Title art: convert to Krill dispatch.
4. Decompressor + phase packing: out of scope, separate follow-up beads.

Fastload smoke and REU runtime suite green with updated expectations. kernal fallback path (no Krill files / failed install) unchanged. No KERNAL file I/O attempted on the boot drive while drive code is installed.
notes:
Quick design pass (2026-09-14):

Most read-path plumbing already exists: overlay_load_disk and tier_load_disk converge on hal_asset_load_prg_header, which dispatches to Krill while krill_active bit 7 is set. Remaining direct read exception: hal_asset_load_title still uses KERNAL and must gain a Krill-active path.

Runtime safety work: hal_asset_krill_call currently runs with display and IRQs active. It should preserve $D011 and caller interrupt state, blank the display, SEI around loadraw, preserve Krill status in A as well as carry, restore $01/$DD00/display, then restore interrupt state. Current flag-preservation logic destroys A, so status-to-UX mapping is not yet possible. Map the complete loader.inc status range, not only the constants currently copied into config.s.

Major scope finding: wrapping only save_game/load_game is insufficient. Any KERNAL IEC transaction asserts ATN; the installed 1541 drive code treats ATN as automatic uninstall (tools/krill/loader/src/drives/drivecode1541.s idleloop41). This includes Disk Setup/device probes, marker I/O, save/load streams, high-score I/O, current title loading, and KERNAL traffic to a second drive. Host state must become inactive before such traffic or a later Krill dispatch can call a stock-DOS drive and hang.

The existing krill_boot_finish cannot be reused at runtime because it is in init-only memory beyond program_end and is overwritten by the dungeon map. A runtime disable helper must live in resident owned memory and use the proven dummy 64.BANK load + uninstall busy-window sequence. RuntimeBanked is effectively full: build/c64/64.bank is 4088 bytes including its PRG header, leaving approximately four payload bytes below $FFFA.

Strict whole-session reinstall is not already solved. build/c64/kinst64.prg is 6998 bytes and loads at $2000, which would overwrite the running game; there is no currently owned 7 KB executable runtime window compatible with KERNAL+I/O visibility. Reinstall therefore needs a separately designed compact drive-type-specific reinstall capsule or new memory ownership.

Recommended minimal scope: keep krill_active=$ff after boot; route title/overlay/tier reads through hardened Krill dispatch; before the first standard-DOS transaction, run a resident krill_disable_for_kernal boundary and permanently degrade to KERNAL for that session. A successful in-game save quits, so reinstall is unnecessary on that common path. Strict persistence after load, failed save, Disk Setup, or high-score I/O should be a prerequisite/subtask rather than assumed wiring.

Verification additions: fastload smoke must execute a real post-title gameplay overlay and tier load through KRILL_LOAD_FILE, assert preserved status/carry and fallback state, retain missing-Krill fallback coverage, run existing scripted save/load and REU suites, and include a standard-DOS transition smoke proving no stale Krill dispatch occurs after uninstall.

Decision required: accept safe permanent fallback after first standard DOS I/O (recommended minimal design), or require strict whole-session persistence and first design the compact runtime reinstaller.
Design Review (moria8-c3r.2) Amendments:
1. IEC ATN line is shared across all drives; ANY KERNAL IEC call (including device 9) uninstalls Krill on drive 8. Suspend is required before ANY KERNAL I/O regardless of target device.
2. Resident memory below $C000 is 100% full (program_end = $C000). Place krill_suspend and krill_resume in ModalMiscOverlay (ovl.modal, ~410 B free) alongside save.s, disk_swap.s, and title_screen.s. Any resident growth for hal_asset_load_title dispatch must be budget-neutral.
3. Preserve Krill status code in A alongside Carry in hal_asset_krill_call.
4. Test plan must include second-drive save + subsequent drive 8 read, and resume graceful degradation on wrong/missing disk.
